findings.title: Login cache keeps stale IDP data after updates that leave login availability unchanged
findings.body:
In `update()`, `registerIDPLoginInvalidationOnUpdate` skips invalidating the login caches when an IDP stays login-eligible with the same organization. The cached query stores only internal IDs, and those are re-resolved through `getById`, so changed attributes like the display name are picked up. Ordering and membership stay correct too.

The gap is the `getById` path: `update()` calls `getById(model.getInternalId())`, which can return an org-aware wrapped model. The predicate is tested against that wrapper, whose `isEnabled()` also depends on the organization being enabled. So the decision to skip invalidation is based on org state, not only on the IDP's own fields.

The cached list is also not invalidated when an organization is disabled or enabled. That is why the bean has to re-check `isEnabled()`. However, the `onlyRealmBrokers` path in `OrganizationAwareIdentityProviderBean` (line 58) does not re-check it.

findings.title: Login cache not invalidated when organization is removed or IDP is unlinked via org provider
findings.body:
The `ORG_ONLY` and `ALL` login caches are keyed only by realm and fetch mode. Invalidation happens only from this provider's `create`, `update` and `remove`.

Removing an organization or deleting its IDPs through other paths, such as `removeAll` on realm deletion, never registers a login-cache invalidation. The `getById` null check only catches IDPs that have been deleted outright.

When an organization is removed but its IDPs remain, possibly unlinked, the cached `ALL`/`ORG_ONLY` results can still include IDPs that are no longer org-linked. The `REALM_ONLY` results can also miss IDPs that should now appear there.

findings.title: Cleanup registers removal of literal alias "alias"
findings.body: Each cleanup is registered with `get("alias")::remove` instead of the actual alias created in the loop. As a result, the created IDPs are never removed, and test state leaks into other tests. The same mistake appears at line 425.
